chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'God refuses repentance for the one who practices innovation (bid'ah).'
It was said: 'O Messenger of God, how is that so?' He said: 'Indeed his heart has been made to drink of its love.'

key_terms.أُشْرِبَ: Was made to drink — a Quranic metaphor (cf. 2:93) for deep internalization. The heart 'drinking' something signifies it has become thoroughly absorbed in the soul.
key_terms.الْبِدْعَةِ: Bid'ah: religious innovation, the introduction of new practices into religion not established by the Prophet or Imams. Considered a grave sin in Shia tradition.

ai.seo_question: Why does God refuse repentance for the innovator according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warns that God refuses the repentance of one who introduces heretical innovations into the religion (bid'ah). When asked why this is so, the Prophet explains that the innovator's heart has been so thoroughly saturated with love for the innovation that genuine repentance becomes impossible. This hadith reflects early Islamic concern with protecting the integrity of religious practice and the psychological mechanism by which sin entrenches itself.
